chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever shaves his head or plucks his armpit hair out of forgetfulness, or heedlessness, or ignorance, there is no penalty upon him; and whoever does it deliberately, upon him is the blood (diyah).'
ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim who shaves their head accidentally versus deliberately?
ai.summary: Reported by the prominent jurist Zurarah from Imam al-Baqir, this hadith establishes the principle of *al-akhthar* (mistake) in Hajj jurisprudence, distinguishing between negligence and intentional violation of the *shurut* (conditions) of consecration. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on intent (*niyyah*) in determining liability, where unintentional acts like shaving or plucking hair incur no penalty, while deliberate acts require *dam* (sacrificial animal). This ruling serves as a foundational text for understanding the flexibility of ritual law when errors occur during the sacred state.
